feed.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion

entry.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
entry.summary:
Analysis of Bitmain hardware reveals a practical limitation on the number of outputs that can be supported, with evidence suggesting that a maximum of 25 outputs is realistic. Examination of recent Ocean pool coinbase transactions demonstrates a notably low number of outputs, which provides insight into current operational constraints.
Ocean’s method for assigning coinbase outputs relies on device fingerprinting and attempts to maximize the number of outputs up to the limits imposed by their firmware. This approach appears to reflect the broader landscape of hardware capabilities, although there may have been changes to these practices over time. The actual output distributions in Ocean’s blocks serve as an approximate indicator of what hardware configurations are prevalent within the network.
For future implementations, such as p2poolv2, it will likely be necessary to reduce the upper limit for outputs below 25. An upper bound of 16 outputs may be more appropriate to ensure compatibility across the majority of devices. Attached histograms and bucket share visualizations illustrate the distribution patterns observed in the data, highlighting the predominance of lower output counts in real-world scenarios.
